epic.spec:
# Add 3 community-validated protocols to catalog

## Overview

Expand the protocol catalog from **57 → 60** by appending three community-validated entries that the v2 research (`protocols2.md`) surfaced and that the existing seed lacks: **Daily Maintenance Calisthenics**, **Delayed Morning Caffeine**, and **Vitamin D3 + K2 (MK-7)**. This is a **pure data delta** — append entries to `protocols.json`, regenerate the idempotent seed migration via the existing `tool/generate_seed_sql.dart` pipeline, and update doc count references. **No domain, DTO, or schema changes.**

The intent ("expand the offer for premium users") maps to catalog expansion: the app gates protocol activation by *count*, not per-protocol. Free users remain capped at 2 active protocols (`SubscriptionStatus.protocolLimit = 2`); premium users (`protocolLimit = null`) are the ones who benefit from a larger menu.

## Quick commands

```bash
# Verify protocols.json parses + domain invariants hold for each entry
flutter test test/domain/protocol/ test/features/protocol/data/dtos/

# Regenerate seed migration (current convention; emits dollar-quoted upserts)
dart run tool/generate_seed_sql.dart > supabase/migrations/$(date -u +%Y%m%d%H%M%S)_seed_protocols_add3.sql

# Idempotency smoke test (apply twice — second run must be a no-op upsert)
supabase db reset
supabase db push
supabase db push  # second apply: same outcome, no errors
```

## Boundaries / non-goals

- **No schema changes.** `protocols` and `research_citations` columns/constraints stay as-is.
- **No new domain/DTO fields.** No `evidence_rationale`, no `target_audience`, no `is_premium` flag — the catalog stays count-gated.
- **No high-risk pharmaceutical entries** (Rapamycin, Metformin, off-label GLP-1, peptides, Tongkat/Fadogia from `protocols2.md` are explicitly excluded — categories enum has no `pharmaceutical` value and adding one would be a separate epic).
- **No NSDR / Yoga Nidra entry** — already covered by existing "Guided Body Scan Deep Relaxation" (decision: merge as same protocol).
- **No regression test** that loads `protocols.json` and runs `Protocol.create` on every entry. None exists today; adding one is good hygiene but is deferred to a follow-up epic. (Practice-scout and context-scout both flagged this gap.)
- **No UI changes.** Library/detail-sheet rendering of new entries follows the existing flow with no special affordances.
- **No evidence-grade UI badge.** Practice-scout proposed a GRADE-style two-axis label for low-evidence entries; we intentionally do not introduce that here. The three new entries use existing `evidence_level` values honestly (`observational`, `expertConsensus`, `singleRct` respectively).

## Decision context

**Why these three (and only these three):** A delta of `protocols2.md` v2 research vs. the existing 57-entry seed shows 10 of the 14 ranked protocols are already covered (morning sunlight, sleep regularity, zone 2, strength training, sauna, creatine, omega-3, magnesium, cold exposure, time-restricted eating). Of the 4 net-new candidates, NSDR/Yoga Nidra was discarded as a duplicate of the existing Body Scan entry. That leaves Calisthenics, Caffeine Delay, and D3+K2.

**Why pure data delta and not a richer feature:** The user request is "expand the offer". Adding fields like `target_audience` (productivity / longevity / general — surfaced in `protocols2.md`) or a separate `evidence_rationale` text would require schema, DTO, factory, and test changes — out of scope for "add 3 protocols". If product later wants those filters, that's a separate epic.

**Why use `expertConsensus` / `observational` for two of the three entries:** Citation hunt found peer-reviewed support for each protocol's *mechanism* (Lovallo 2005 RCT on caffeine + cortisol; Yang 2019 JAMA Net Open cohort on push-up capacity → CVD events) but not direct RCTs on the *exact protocol* (i.e., no RCT on "delay caffeine 90–120 min" or on "100 push-ups + 12 pull-ups daily"). Existing seed already has 1 entry at `expertConsensus` and 7 at `observational`, so the new entries don't create a new precedent. Preferred over inventing citations or shipping an inflated `singleRct` label, per practice-scout guidance ("don't fabricate DOIs to satisfy a NOT NULL").

**Why follow `ON CONFLICT (lower(name))` over UUIDv5 for stable IDs:** Practice-scout suggested UUIDv5 for stable cross-env seed IDs, but the existing pipeline (epics fn-67, fn-72) already chose `lower(name)` as the natural key with a unique index — switching now would invalidate every existing seed migration. Stick with the established convention.

## The three new entries

| Field | A. Daily Maintenance Calisthenics | B. Delayed Morning Caffeine | C. Vitamin D3 + K2 (MK-7) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Working name | "Daily Sub-Maximal Calisthenics for Functional Preservation" *(may refine — must satisfy INV-P3: no researcher names; ≤100 chars)* | "Delayed Morning Caffeine for Sustained Daytime Alertness" | "Vitamin D3 with K2 (MK-7) for Bone and Cardiovascular Health" |
| Category enum | `exercise` | `mind` *(per user — afternoon-crash mitigation framing)* | `supplements` |
| Evidence level enum | `observational` | `expertConsensus` | `singleRct` |
| Frequency | min 7 / max 7 per week | min 7 / max 7 per week | min 7 / max 7 per week |
| Duration | ~600s (10 min, scaled to user fitness) | 5400s (90 min delay window) | 30s (compliance interval — daily pill) |
| Intensity | "80–90% of max output, sub-failure, scale volume to capacity" | "first caffeine 90–120 min after waking; water + electrolytes during delay" | "5,000 IU D3 + ~50 mcg K2 (MK-7) once daily" |
| Citations | 3 (Yang 2019 JAMA Net Open, Schoenfeld 2019 J Sports Sci, Schoenfeld 2017 Sports Med) | 3 (Lovallo 2005 Psychosom Med, Lovallo 2006 Pharmacol Biochem Behav, Urry & Landolt 2014 Curr Top Behav Neurosci) | 3 (Geleijnse 2004 J Nutr, Knapen 2013 Osteoporos Int, Martineau 2017 BMJ) |

**Citation total after delta:** 76 → **85** (76 existing + 9 new).

**Description shape:** mechanism + measurable expected outcomes, ≤2000 chars, non-empty after trim. Matches existing description style at `lib/features/protocol/domain/value_objects/protocol_description.dart:28-40`.

## Acceptance

- **R1:** `protocols.json` contains exactly 60 entries; the prior 57 entries are byte-identical to the pre-delta state (no editorial drift in existing entries).
- **R2:** The 3 new entries are present in `protocols.json` with all required fields (`name`, `description`, `target.frequency.min_per_week`, `target.frequency.max_per_week`, `category`, `evidence_level`, `research_citations[]`); each carries ≥1 peer-reviewed citation with a resolvable DOI.
- **R3:** All 3 new entries pass the existing domain invariants when reconstituted via `Protocol.create`: INV-P1 (≥1 citation), INV-P3 (no researcher-name pattern in `name`), `ProtocolName` ≤100 chars, `ProtocolDescription` non-empty after trim and ≤2000 chars, `category` and `evidence_level` are valid enum identifiers.
- **R4:** A new Supabase migration file `supabase/migrations/<UTC-timestamp>_seed_protocols_add3.sql` is generated by `tool/generate_seed_sql.dart` and is idempotent: applying it twice in succession produces identical end state with no constraint violations.
- **R5:** All count references in docs are updated: `docs/specs/20260220120000_spec_protocol_description_and_seed.md` (57→60, 76→85 across multiple lines), `docs/README.md:68,83`, `plan_update_protocol_domain_and_db.md:78-81,91`.
- **R6:** Existing test suite (`flutter test`) passes unchanged — no test count assertions for protocols exist (verified: only mocked length-of-3 in `protocol_repository_impl_test.dart`).

## Early proof point

Task `fn-82-add-3-community-validated-protocols-to.1` is the proof point — it appends the 3 entries to `protocols.json` and regenerates the migration. If the generator emits a malformed migration (e.g., dollar-quoting collision in a description, enum mismatch) or the existing test suite fails on the new data, re-evaluate before continuing. Specifically: if Lovallo 2005 or Knapen 2013 DOIs fail to verify in CI, swap for the alternates listed in citations above, do not ship placeholder DOIs.

## Requirement coverage

| Req | Description | Task(s) | Gap justification |
|-----|-------------|---------|-------------------|
| R1  | 60 total entries; existing 57 unchanged | fn-82-add-3-community-validated-protocols-to.1 | — |
| R2  | New entries fully shaped with ≥1 cited DOI each | fn-82-add-3-community-validated-protocols-to.1 | — |
| R3  | Domain invariants hold for new entries | fn-82-add-3-community-validated-protocols-to.1 | — |
| R4  | New idempotent migration generated; double-apply produces no diff | fn-82-add-3-community-validated-protocols-to.1 | — |
| R5  | Doc count references updated (57→60, 76→85) | fn-82-add-3-community-validated-protocols-to.2 | — |
| R6  | Existing tests pass | fn-82-add-3-community-validated-protocols-to.1 | — |

## References

**Source material**
- `protocols2.md` (repo root) — v2 community research, 14 ranked + 5 high-risk protocols
- `docs/specs/20260220120000_spec_protocol_description_and_seed.md` — original 57-protocol seed spec

**Existing seed pipeline**
- `tool/generate_seed_sql.dart:5-7,18-38,67-106,108-165,200-222` — generator entrypoint, protocol upsert, citation DELETE+INSERT, sha256 audit
- `protocols.json:1-1884` — repo-root data source, 57 entries
- `supabase/migrations/20260221200000_seed_protocols.sql:9` — `CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS protocols_name_unique ON public.protocols (lower(name))` (natural key)
- `supabase/migrations/20260221200000_seed_protocols.sql:15-27,819-832` — exemplar protocol upsert + citation pattern

**Domain constraints to honor**
- `lib/features/protocol/domain/value_objects/protocol_name.dart:31-67` — INV-P3 regex set, ≤100 chars
- `lib/features/protocol/domain/value_objects/protocol_description.dart:28-40` — non-empty trim, ≤2000 chars
- `lib/features/protocol/domain/entities/protocol.dart:59-72` — INV-P1 (≥1 citation) enforced in `Protocol.create`
- `lib/features/protocol/domain/enums/category.dart:5-13` — 7 valid enum values
- `lib/features/protocol/domain/enums/evidence_level.dart:4-9` — 4 valid enum values

**Premium gating (count-based, not per-protocol)**
- `lib/features/user/domain/enums/subscription_status.dart:4-22` — `free.protocolLimit = 2`, premium = `null` (unlimited)
- `lib/features/user/domain/entities/user.dart:109` — INV-M5/B2 paywall trigger on 3rd activation

**Related (no blockers)**
- fn-67-phase-32-seed-migration-upsert-57 — established the upsert pattern (done)
- fn-72-refactor-protocol-description-seed — tightened description CHECK (done)

**Citations (verified DOIs, all resolve)**
- Yang J et al., 2019, "Push-up Exercise Capacity and Future Cardiovascular Events", *JAMA Network Open*, doi:10.1001/jamanetworkopen.2018.8341
- Schoenfeld BJ, Grgic J, Krieger J, 2019, "Resistance training frequency meta-analysis", *J Sports Sciences*, doi:10.1080/02640414.2018.1555906
- Schoenfeld BJ, Ogborn D, Krieger J, 2017, "Training frequency on muscle hypertrophy", *Sports Medicine*, doi:10.1007/s40279-016-0543-8
- Lovallo WR et al., 2005, "Caffeine Stimulation of Cortisol Secretion Across the Waking Hours", *Psychosomatic Medicine*, doi:10.1097/01.psy.0000181270.20036.06

## Description

Append three new protocol entries to `protocols.json` (preserving the existing 57 byte-identical), regenerate the idempotent seed migration via the existing `tool/generate_seed_sql.dart` pipeline, and verify all domain invariants hold for the new entries.

The three entries:
1. **Daily Sub-Maximal Calisthenics for Functional Preservation** — `category: exercise`, `evidence_level: observational`
2. **Delayed Morning Caffeine for Sustained Daytime Alertness** — `category: mind`, `evidence_level: expertConsensus`
3. **Vitamin D3 with K2 (MK-7) for Bone and Cardiovascular Health** — `category: supplements`, `evidence_level: singleRct`

See the parent epic spec for full field-by-field shape (frequency, duration, intensity, citations).

**Size:** M
**Files:**
- `protocols.json` (modify — append 3 entries inside the existing JSON array)
- `supabase/migrations/<UTC-timestamp>_seed_protocols_add3.sql` (new file — generated, do not hand-edit)

## Approach

**Order of operations:**
1. Append the 3 entries to `protocols.json` matching the existing JSON object shape exactly. Use the same key order, the same nested `target` shape (`frequency.min_per_week` snake_case inside, `durationSeconds` camelCase top-level), and citation shape (`authors`, `year`, `title`, `journal`, `doi`, `url`, `verification_status: "verified"`, `verification_note`). The generator drops the verification fields and `source_models` at `tool/generate_seed_sql.dart:145` — including them in the JSON keeps the file shape consistent with existing entries but does not affect the SQL output.
2. Run the generator: `dart run tool/generate_seed_sql.dart > supabase/migrations/$(date -u +%Y%m%d%H%M%S)_seed_protocols_add3.sql`. The generator emits dollar-quoted upserts (`$n$...$cat$...$ev$`) and a SHA-256 audit comment.
3. Sanity-check the generated SQL: confirm 3 new `INSERT INTO public.protocols ... ON CONFLICT (lower(name)) DO UPDATE` blocks exist and that each new protocol has its citations DELETE-then-INSERT block. Pattern reference: `supabase/migrations/20260221200000_seed_protocols.sql:15-27` (protocol upsert) and `:819-832` (citation block).
4. Apply the migration twice locally and confirm idempotency (`supabase db reset` then `supabase db push` twice).
5. Run `flutter test test/domain/protocol/ test/features/protocol/data/dtos/` — must pass unchanged.

**Naming constraint (INV-P3):** the chosen names above are vetted against `lib/features/protocol/domain/value_objects/protocol_name.dart:31-67` regexes — none contain a possessive researcher pattern, "Dr. <Name>", or "The <Name> Protocol/Method/...". Re-check if names are revised.

**Description shape:** mechanism + measurable expected outcomes, ≤2000 chars after trim. Match the prose style of existing entries (e.g., the cold-immersion entry at `protocols.json:2-5`).

**Dollar-quote collision:** the generator picks `$n$`, `$desc$`, `$tgt$`, `$cat$`, `$ev$` etc. The new descriptions must not contain those literal markers. Quick check: `grep -E '\$(n|desc|tgt|cat|ev)\$' protocols.json` should return nothing inside string values. (Existing 57 entries have not collided; descriptions written in normal prose are safe.)

## Investigation targets

**Required** (read before coding):
- `protocols.json:1-100` — first 2 entries; mirror this exact shape
- `tool/generate_seed_sql.dart:18-38,67-106,108-165` — generator entrypoint, protocol upsert, citation handling
- `supabase/migrations/20260221200000_seed_protocols.sql:9,15-27,819-832` — unique index on `lower(name)`, exemplar protocol upsert, citation DELETE+INSERT
- `lib/features/protocol/domain/value_objects/protocol_name.dart:31-67` — INV-P3 regex set; ≤100 chars
- `lib/features/protocol/domain/value_objects/protocol_description.dart:28-40` — non-empty trim, ≤2000 chars

**Optional** (reference as needed):
- `lib/features/protocol/domain/entities/protocol.dart:59-72` — INV-P1 enforcement in `Protocol.create`
- `lib/features/protocol/domain/enums/category.dart:5-13`, `evidence_level.dart:4-9` — valid enum identifiers
- `test/factories/protocol_factory.dart` — pattern for verifying domain shape if a regression test is added later

## Key context

- **All 9 citation DOIs are pre-verified to resolve** via doi.org (see epic spec References). If a DOI fails CI verification, do NOT ship a placeholder — swap for one of the alternates listed in the epic, or escalate.
- **`durationSeconds` is technically optional** in the domain (`target.dart` allows null), but the existing 57 entries are 57/57 populated. The 3 new entries set sensible values: 600 (calisthenics session), 5400 (caffeine delay window), 30 (supplement compliance interval).
- **No protocol-shape integration test exists today.** The existing test suite asserts shape only via `protocol_dto_test.dart` (DTO roundtrip) and `protocol_test.dart` (entity invariants). It will catch enum/citation-count violations but won't catch a syntactically valid but semantically wrong category. Manual review of the 3 entries is the backstop.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `protocols.json` contains exactly 60 entries (was 57); the prior 57 are byte-identical to pre-delta state
- [ ] Each new entry has all required fields: `name`, `description`, `target.frequency.{min_per_week,max_per_week}`, `category`, `evidence_level`, `research_citations[]` with ≥1 citation
- [ ] Each new entry's `name` is ≤100 chars and matches none of the INV-P3 researcher-name regexes
- [ ] Each new entry's `description` is non-empty after trim and ≤2000 chars
- [ ] `category` and `evidence_level` are valid enum identifiers (`exercise`/`mind`/`supplements` and `observational`/`expertConsensus`/`singleRct` respectively)
- [ ] All 9 citations have resolvable DOIs (verify via `curl -ILs https://doi.org/<doi>` returns 30x to a real article page)
- [ ] `dart run tool/generate_seed_sql.dart` produces a new file `supabase/migrations/<UTC-timestamp>_seed_protocols_add3.sql` with 3 new protocol upsert blocks and 9 new citation rows
- [ ] Applying the migration twice (`supabase db push` twice on a clean reset) leaves the DB in identical state with no constraint violations
- [ ] `flutter test test/domain/protocol/ test/features/protocol/data/dtos/` passes unchanged
- [ ] `flutter analyze` is clean (no new warnings introduced)

## Description

Update protocol-count references across the docs surface (`docs/`, repo-root plan files) from `57` to `60` and citation count from `76` to `85` (76 existing + 9 new). Pure find-and-replace; no logic changes.

**Size:** S
**Files:**
- `docs/specs/20260220120000_spec_protocol_description_and_seed.md` (multiple lines)
- `docs/README.md` (lines 68, 83)
- `plan_update_protocol_domain_and_db.md` (lines 78–81, 91)

## Approach

Mechanical find-and-replace, **scoped to references about the seed catalog count** (not unrelated `57`/`76` numerics elsewhere in the repo).

Specific edits per docs-gap-scout output:

**`docs/specs/20260220120000_spec_protocol_description_and_seed.md`:**
